idiom_name: transition table of {action function pointer, next state} indexed by state x signal
implementation_notes: C's standard library ships no flow machinery, so the Application Controller is written as data: an enum of states, an enum of signals, and a two-dimensional table whose rows hold an action function pointer plus the next state; one dispatch function looks up the row for (state, signal), calls the action through the pointer and stores the next state. The classic object form (polymorphic command objects with a view registry) is replaced by this table plus an enum of screen ids that the caller renders; keep the table form as long as the flow is fixed at compile time and the commands are functions over one context struct, and move to generated code or a scripting layer only when the flow must be reconfigured without recompiling.
pitfalls: The enums and the table dimensions must stay in sync: a missing row is a silently zero-initialised entry, so build the table with designated initializers and assert its size with _Static_assert (C11).
A NULL action is indistinguishable from an unhandled (state, signal) pair; make every entry explicit, or treat NULL as an error with a logged transition instead of a no-op.
File-scope flow state (a static Ctx) makes the controller single-user and non-reentrant; pass the context in, and keep per-conversation data in the caller's struct.
